column2: Pessimistic concurrency control locks a record as soon as a transaction reads it, so nobody else can change it until the transaction finishes. It is safe when conflicts are frequent but it reduces throughput and can cause deadlocks. Optimistic control lets everyone read without locks and checks a version number or timestamp at commit time, rolling back if someone else changed the row. It works well when conflicts are rare because there is no waiting, but retries become expensive under heavy contention.

column2: An index is a data structure like a B-tree that lets the database find rows without scanning the whole table, so reads and searches become much faster. The cost is that every insert, update or delete must also update the index, so writes get slower and the index uses extra storage. So we index columns used often in where clauses and joins, but we avoid indexing everything.
